title: SIREN: Software Identification and Recognition in HPC Systems
problem: HPC systems rely on monitoring and analytics for efficiency and security, but lack reliable software identification methods. Job/file names unreliable (user-provided). Application-specific insights hindered by inability to identify unknown software or recognize repeated executions across runs.
method: SIREN: Process-level data collection framework using fuzzy hashing of executable contents. Detects software similarity despite version differences or different compilation approaches. Collects process metadata, environment info, executable fuzzy hashes. Deployed on LUMI (opt-in) to demonstrate effectiveness on real HPC workloads.

title: N-Well Patterning of P-Type CMOS Substrate for Improving Quality Factor of on-Chip Inductors at Millimeter Wave Frequencies
problem: On-chip inductors at mmW frequencies suffer from eddy current and capacitive coupling losses
method: N-well patterning on p-type substrate; two patterning structures reduce eddy/capacitive currents in spiral inductors

title: Enhancing Digital Microfluidic Biochip Operations with Scheduling Interval Method
problem: Digital Microfluidic Biochip (DMFB) sample preparation involves complex mixing sequences with constraints on fluid usage, mixer availability, storage capacity, and chemical waste. Existing scheduling algorithms do not jointly optimize all these parameters.
method: Interval-based scheduling algorithm for DMFB sample preparation that minimizes: (1) input pipes, (2) mixer units, (3) storage units, (4) mixing counts, (5) storage counts, (6) fluid shifting operations. Evaluated against Reservoir Minimizing Scheduling (RMS) baseline.

title: Insights from Rights and Wrongs: A Large Language Model for Solving Assertion Failures in RTL Design
problem: SystemVerilog assertion failures in RTL simulation require manual analysis of complex signal timing and logic relationships; no automated tool exists to diagnose and fix failures.
method: AssertSolver is an LLM fine-tuned on synthetic SVA failure-fix pairs and learns from error feedback. Given an assertion failure, the model generates diagnostic code and proposed design fixes.

title: Secondary-Power-Cell-Aware Detailed Placement in Multiple Power Domain Designs
problem: Cross-domain cells in multi-power-domain designs require secondary power routing that competes with signal routing; strict IR drop constraints at advanced nodes make placement for efficient secondary PDN difficult.
method: Integer linear programming (ILP) model for detailed placement accounting for secondary power routing; targeted adjustments to cross-domain cell placement; validated against commercial tools.

title: DROIDFUZZ: Proprietary Driver Fuzzing for Embedded Android Devices
problem: Embedded Android devices (smart home, automotive, IoT) require security validation, but traditional kernel testing cannot reach vendor-specific driver logic in the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL). Proprietary drivers are black-boxes; standard fuzzing frameworks cannot effectively probe HAL/kernel boundaries.
method: DroidFuzz, an embedded Android system fuzzer targeting vendor-specific driver implementations. Uses pre-testing HAL driver probing to identify driver interfaces, kernel-user relational payload generation to craft valid cross-boundary inputs, and cross-boundary execution state feedback to guide fuzzing toward deeper driver logic. Simultaneously tests kernel and HAL layers.

title: A GPU FFT Wrapper to Co-optimize Floating-Point Precision and Library Selection via Predictive Error Modeling
problem: FFT libraries exhibit different performance-accuracy tradeoffs at different scales and precisions; selecting optimal library+precision combination requires manual exploration or expensive profiling
method: ML-based wrapper library that samples input features, predicts per-kernel error via lightweight model, selects library+precision minimizing runtime/energy while meeting error threshold

title: MEEK: Re-thinking Heterogeneous Parallel Error Detection Architecture for Real-World OoO Superscalar Processors
problem: Heterogeneous parallel error detection requires gathering data cross-chip from many core components to re-execute software, but integrating this into commodity out-of-order superscalar cores creates design complexity and risks heavy modifications to mature microarchitectures.
method: MEEK implements heterogeneous parallel error detection via co-designed hardware-software layers: a high-performance OoO core executes speculatively while power-efficient auxiliary cores re-execute the same code; coordinating software and light OS-level modifications orchestrate comparison and error reporting with microsecond-level latency. The design avoids invasive changes by partitioning responsibilities across ISA, microarchitecture, and operating system.

title: Bishop: Sparsified Bundling Spiking Transformers on Heterogeneous Cores with Error-constrained Pruning
problem: Spiking transformers combine attention mechanisms with spike-based computation, but their large size and high spatiotemporal volume of computation make efficient hardware acceleration difficult due to variable activation sparsity and the inefficiency of treating attention's binary spike operations with conventional accelerator designs.
method: Bishop introduces the Token-Time Bundle (TTB) container that groups spike data across tokens and time steps for efficient packing. A heterogeneous accelerator routes high-density TTBs to a dense core array and low-density TTBs to a sparse core array via a stratifier. BSA (Bundle Sparsity-Aware) training improves structured TTB-level firing sparsity. ECP (Error-Constrained TTB Pruning) trims spiking query/key/value activations with a provable error bound before and after attention map computation. A reconfigurable TTB spiking attention core executes attention as AND-and-Accumulate operations on binary spikes.

title: GLiTCH: GLiTCH induced Transitions for Secure Crypto-Hardware
problem: Power side-channel attacks exploit dynamic power profiles to infer cryptographic keys; conventional glitch reduction improves power efficiency but overlooks that strategic glitch manipulation can reduce correlation between power consumption and secret data.
method: GLiTCH framework combines addition and removal of glitches via gate-sizing-based arrival time control, formulated as a Geometric Programming optimization problem. Framework is guided by functional and timing simulations to validate correctness and performance. Applied to AES, CLEFIA, and SM4 cipher designs to reduce power side-channel leakage.

title: MeHyper: Accelerating Hypergraph Neural Networks by Exploring Implicit Dataflows
problem: Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) based on hyperedge-centric dataflow independently process vertex and hyperedge aggregation tasks, causing significant computational redundancy from recalculating shared information (intermediate feature values) across these tasks.
method: MeHyper introduces a microedge concept that captures fine-grained shared information between aggregation tasks, replacing the hyperedge-centric model with a microedge-centric dataflow that processes shared information once and distributes it to all dependent tasks. The execution follows a Read-Process-Activate-Generate model optimized for parallel microedge task processing. The hardware accelerator features a decoupled pipeline for improved computational parallelism and a hierarchical feature management strategy that partitions on-chip memory across feature granularities to reduce off-chip DRAM accesses for the large intermediate feature vectors generated during microedge aggregation.

title: StreamHub: High-performance Managed SciStream as a Service
problem: Real-time transfer and analysis of high-throughput scientific data to remote facilities
method: Zero-trust streaming infrastructure integrating Globus Compute

title: RE3: Finding Refinement Relations with Relational Mapping Abstraction
problem: Manually constructing refinement relations between sequential circuits is tedious and error-prone, requiring deep domain knowledge and formal methods expertise, especially for post-transformation designs.
method: Develops rigorous sequential equivalence checking algorithm that automatically discovers concise, human-comprehensible refinement relations between two non-cycle-accurate designs using relational mapping abstraction.

title: A Cutting-Edge Parallel Solver for Scalable Power Grid Analysis Using Nested Domain Decomposition
problem: Modern power distribution networks at sub-5nm nodes contain billions to trillions of nodes with reduced noise margins and high power density, creating massive sparse linear systems that conventional domain decomposition methods cannot solve efficiently due to exponentially growing dense Schur complements.
method: Proposes nested domain decomposition solver incorporating parallel Schur complement computation strategy and intermediate Schur complement to reduce the size of the final global Schur complement. The intermediate complement breaks the computation into manageable stages.

title: Treelet Accelerated Ray Tracing on GPUs
problem: GPU ray tracing suffers from poor memory access locality because rays traverse a BVH tree in divergent order, causing excessive DRAM traffic; while treelet-based traversal (grouping BVH subtrees and batching rays per treelet) reduces memory traffic on specialized accelerators, applying it to GPUs is non-trivial and naive implementations are ineffective.
method: The paper proposes Virtualized Treelet Queues with two main components. First, ray virtualization terminates raygen shaders after issuing their trace-ray instruction to free CUDA cores, increasing the number of rays concurrently in flight and enabling more cache reuse within treelets. Second, a dynamic treelet queue architecture switches between traversal modes (intra-treelet vs. inter-treelet) at runtime to maximize efficiency. Additionally, warp repacking is applied to the RT unit to improve SIMT efficiency during treelet traversal.

title: Addressing Reproducibility Challenges in HPC with Continuous Integration
problem: HPC research reproducibility is limited by unique infrastructure access, software complexity, and lack of CI/CD tooling tailored to HPC.
method: CORRECT: GitHub Action enabling secure execution of tests on remote HPC resources; survey of reproducibility initiatives and barriers.
